pages.title: BenchFlow
pages.job: Know in one screen what BenchFlow is, what you can do with it, and which page is your job.

pages.title: Install
pages.job: Install `bench` and the Python package at a pinned version, check the machine, and move between versions.

pages.title: Quick start
pages.job: Score one task with its reference solution, with an agent that does nothing, and with Claude Code, then read the results.

pages.title: How BenchFlow works
pages.job: The rollout, BenchFlow's unit: what goes into one (task, environment, agent, model), what comes out (trajectory, reward, artifacts), and what reads them.

pages.title: Why BenchFlow
pages.job: See what an agent evaluation needs beyond a score, from Han-chung Lee's posts, and which part of BenchFlow answers each need.

pages.title: Find a benchmark
pages.job: See which benchmarks you can run: the registry, any folder of tasks in a Git repository, and your own folders.

pages.title: Agents and models
pages.job: Pick an agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi and more), log in or set a key, and choose the model and effort.

pages.title: Before you run an eval
pages.job: Settle the settings that change a score (harness, effort, sampling, tries, limits, controls, cost) and see the plan before anything runs.

pages.title: Run a benchmark
pages.job: Run an agent on many tasks at once, choose which tasks and how many tries, and know where the results go.

pages.title: Read the results
pages.job: Read a job's score, each trial's outcome and reward, what the agent did and what it cost, from the shell, the browser or Python.

pages.title: When a trial fails
pages.job: Find out why a trial failed or has no score, whose problem it is, and what to do next.

pages.title: Skills
pages.job: Give the agent skills, confirm it used them, and measure whether they help.

pages.title: Run your own agent
pages.job: Score an agent you wrote, over ACP or as a script, like any built-in agent.

pages.title: Embodied tasks (Robo Use)
pages.job: Run Robo Use's simulated robot tasks from several seeds, read the results seed by seed, and give the reference solution its token.

pages.title: Bring what you have
pages.job: Run tasks in the Terminal-Bench (task.toml) format, convert or export them, read old BenchFlow jobs, and hand trajectories to tools that read ATIF; see what doesn't carry over yet.

pages.title: Check a benchmark
pages.job: Before trusting a benchmark's scores, show that every task can be solved, none passes for free, the verifiers hold, and the tasks aren't flaky.

pages.title: Compare runs
pages.job: Pick the metric, count failures the right way, and tell with an interval whether two runs really differ.

pages.title: Reproduce a published score
pages.job: Take a published number, match its settings, rerun it, and say whether it holds.

pages.title: Report a result
pages.job: Publish a score with the settings, controls, intervals and files another researcher needs to check it.

pages.title: Known pitfalls
pages.job: Problems that quietly change a score or break a run, each with its symptom, cause, how to detect it, and the fix.

pages.title: Write a task
pages.job: Write a small research task (data in, a number out, a stated tolerance), check it, prove it with the controls, and run an agent on it.

pages.title: Task format
pages.job: The files of a task, what each is for, and the task.toml layout BenchFlow also reads; where both forms exist, they must match.

pages.title: Multi-turn tasks
pages.job: Give the agent several prompts in one sandbox: a scripted user that writes each next prompt, or several agents taking turns.

pages.title: Multi-step tasks
pages.job: Split a task into steps that are each checked before the next one starts.

pages.title: Verifiers
pages.job: Score a trial with a test script: pass or fail, partial credit, tolerances, and a separate verifier for long tasks.

pages.title: Rubric review
pages.job: Grade the work a test can't check, such as the method behind an answer, with a weighted rubric and a reviewer agent, and read its verdicts.

pages.title: LLM judge
pages.job: Grade what no script can check, a piece of writing or a web page, with a model and criteria you write, and know what the judge records.

pages.title: Human preferences
pages.job: Judge two outputs at a time, blind, live and with reasons, by a person or a model, then rank the agents with intervals.

pages.title: Network and secrets
pages.job: Control what the agent can reach, keep it off the web or away from given sites, and know which keys and files enter the sandbox.

pages.title: Stop reward hacking
pages.job: Make sure an agent can't score without doing the work, and prove it with probes.

pages.title: Publish a benchmark
pages.job: Share a folder of tasks through Git or the registry, version it, and declare the setup runs should match.

pages.title: Sandboxes
pages.job: Choose where trials run, and set up Docker, remote Docker or AgentCore.

pages.title: Daytona
pages.job: Run trials in Daytona cloud sandboxes: setup, limits, and cleanup.

pages.title: Modal
pages.job: Run trials in Modal sandboxes, including tasks that need GPUs.

pages.title: Concurrency and budgets
pages.job: Run many trials at once, cap what a job may spend, and watch a long run.

pages.title: Usage and telemetry
pages.job: What BenchFlow records for every model call (tokens, cost, timing, settings), where each number comes from, and what happens when an agent exports no OpenTelemetry.

pages.title: Resume, retries and regrade
pages.job: Continue a stopped job, know which failures are retried, and rescore saved work with a fixed verifier.

pages.title: Configs and variables
pages.job: Keep a whole run in a YAML file, and send each environment variable where it's needed.

pages.title: Run in CI
pages.job: Run a benchmark in CI and fail the build when the pass rate drops.

pages.title: BenchFlow as an RL environment
pages.job: Run groups of rollouts on a task, score them, and read rewards and advantages, with token capture on from the start.

pages.title: Export training data
pages.job: Turn finished trials into rows a trainer reads, check the rows, and know each file a trial writes for trainers and other tools, with its schema.

pages.title: Connect a trainer
pages.job: Stream rollouts to a trainer while a job runs, check token capture, launch a Prime-RL SFT job, and connect other trainers through files.

pages.title: Upgrade from 0.7
pages.job: Move an install and a project from 0.7.x to 0.9.2, and go back if you need to.

pages.title: What's in 0.10.0rc2
pages.job: The prerelease's features, how to install it, and what may still change.

pages.title: Changelog
pages.job: Every release's changes, from the repository's CHANGELOG.

pages.title: Commands
pages.job: Look up every `bench` command and flag, including the ones `--help` hides and the ones new in 0.10.

pages.title: Python API
pages.job: Look up every public name in the `benchflow` package.

pages.title: CLI and Python
pages.job: Find the Python argument that does what each `bench` flag does.

pages.title: Files BenchFlow reads and writes
pages.job: Look up every key of the task files you write and every field of the job and trial files BenchFlow writes.

pages.title: Error messages
pages.job: Look up a fixed message BenchFlow prints and what to do about it.

pages.title: Environment variables
pages.job: Every variable BenchFlow reads, and where it goes: your machine, the sandbox, the agent or the verifier.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.job: Every term in these docs, one line each, with the page that covers it.
